articles.title: Amazon plans to expand Prime Air to nearly 500 cities by the end of 2026
articles.summary: Amazon plans to expand Prime Air drone delivery to nearly 500 U.S. cities and towns by the end of 2026, a sixfold increase from its current footprint, while also beginning international service in Darlington, U.K. The service can deliver eligible items weighing 5 lb. or less in as fast as 30 minutes and is integrated into Amazon’s existing shopping and checkout experience.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a concrete example of large-scale commercial deployment of autonomous robotics in logistics. For advisors, it highlights how AI-enabled physical automation may reshape last-mile delivery economics, customer expectations, regulatory frameworks, and potential demand for related technologies such as sensors, onboard compute, navigation systems, and electric drone infrastructure.

articles.advisor_relevance: The article points to continued AI feature expansion in everyday knowledge-worker tools, especially document-heavy workflows such as contracts, compliance, and professional services. While the investment read-through is limited by the sparse detail and apparent product-marketing nature of the piece, it supports the broader theme that AI agents are moving from summarization into workflow execution and file manipulation.

articles.title: Mapping General-Purpose AI Governance in Twenty AI Middle-Power Jurisdictions
articles.summary: The paper maps general-purpose AI governance provisions across twenty “AI middle-power” jurisdictions, including the EU, focusing on systemic risk assessment, evaluation and verification, prohibitions with monitoring and detection, and serious incident reporting. It finds broad convergence in governance categories but limited legal force: only about one in five provisions are binding, and outside the EU no jurisdiction imposes a binding evaluation duty on model developers.
articles.advisor_relevance: This matters because AI governance is increasingly global, but the paper suggests most middle-power jurisdictions are building observation and coordination capacity rather than imposing hard obligations on frontier model developers. For advisors, the read-through is that regulatory risk remains uneven and fragmented, with the EU standing out as more forceful while many other jurisdictions may create compliance complexity without yet materially constraining leading AI platforms.

articles.title: ATDev gives update on its journey building autonomous wheelchairs
articles.summary: ATDev is developing an autonomous power wheelchair with a coordinated robotic arm under the ARPA-H-funded RAMMP program led by the University of Pittsburgh. The system is designed for shared autonomy, helping users with reaching, lifting, eating, drinking, opening doors, and potentially teleoperated tasks such as retrieving items from another room. ATDev is also working with Meta to apply AI models to the chairs and is exploring federated learning so chairs can share learned capabilities across users.
articles.advisor_relevance: This article highlights a real-world example of AI and robotics moving into healthcare and assistive mobility, where aging demographics could create long-term demand. While ATDev appears early-stage and the market is constrained by FDA approval and insurance reimbursement, the development points to broader investment themes around physical AI, medical robotics, sensorized mobility platforms, and the use of large AI models in specialized devices.

articles.title: Logic Robotics launches autonomous pallet for rail-to-road transloading

articles.title: Growth Without Us: Machine Consumers, Corporate Circularity, and the Decoupling of GDP from Humanity after AGI
articles.summary: The paper models a hypothetical post-AGI economy where corporations own AI and robotic agents that both produce and consume energy, compute, maintenance, and upgrades. It argues that growth could become decoupled from human labor and consumption, with the key constraint shifting to fabrication throughput and energy capture, while human welfare depends primarily on ownership of the corporate network.
articles.advisor_relevance: This is a speculative framework rather than a concrete market development, but it highlights long-term AI investment questions around who owns productive AI assets, how energy and compute constraints could shape growth, and why capital ownership may matter more than employment in highly automated scenarios.

articles.title: Liquid AI Releases LFM2.5-DSpark Draft Models That Deliver Up to 3.18x Faster Decoding Without Changing Model Outputs
